result:
**Verdict: FAIL.** The only reason is that my round-6 finding F-DG4-148 is not fixed, and the assignment allows PASS only if all three of my round-6 findings close. I raised no new findings.

I confirmed the candidate (`sha256:baa6ff4d…`, 1475 files) on a complete clone at `dab4562`, at the start and at the end.

**Round-6 findings** (in `qa-verifier.verifications.json`)

| Finding | Result | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **F-DG4-146** (Low) | PASS, CLOSED_VERIFIED | My mutant M4 makes 6 tests of the new `session-wait.test.tsx` fail. Each split mutant makes one fail: M4a fails W4, M4b fails W3. The unmutated baseline passes 86/86. |
| **F-DG4-147** (Low) | PASS, CLOSED_VERIFIED | I delayed the boot `GET /me` by 1.5 s or 4 s. The pre-repair test then fails 12/12 with the round-6 error (expected 403, got 200), and the repaired test passes 12/12. The repaired test also passed 10 repeats per language at load 5–9 and again with load held at 13–17 (20/20 each). |
| **F-DG4-148** (Low, not mandatory) | **FAIL, stays OPEN** | The two harness changes work and weaken no test, but `pnpm test` still fails under load. Details below. |

**F-DG4-148 detail**
- **What works:**
  - The split test script runs all three test groups and exits 1 if any one fails, including a failure only in the last group (checked at low load).
  - The warm-up does not bypass the loading fallback: if I remove the fallback, 4 tests fail with the warm-up still on.
- **What still fails:**
  - **At the load of three concurrent reviews (22–30):** 3 of 4 runs exit 1.
  - **With load held at 13–16** (median 15.5 during the failing run, inside the band the fix claimed): 1 of 4 runs exits 1.
  - **The failures are the finding's two classes:**
    - `apps/api/src/architecture.test.ts` takes 33–41 s against its 30 s limit.
    - The first render of the actions page in `raid.test.tsx` "action register" (en) misses its 5 s wait, even with the page module warmed.
  - **At low load (2–5):** 4 of 4 runs pass.
- **Likely reason the fix's own evidence differs:** its load was pure CPU busy loops, while mine also included a browser test run, as the real review process does.
- **The product is unaffected.**

**Rest of the review (all PASS)**
- **Static checks:** all 7 exit 0.
- **Integration:** two runs, 1984/1984 each. That covers 61 migrations, `contract.test.ts` and the new worker `supervise-cadence.test.ts` (9/9), with every p4-pending list empty. The assignment says migrations go to 0060; the candidate actually ships 0061.
- **QA suites:** `tests/qa` alone passes 172/172.
- **REQ-DLV-036:** the A04, A09, A10 and A11 suites pass, 85 tests in total.
- **Full e2e:** all 364 tests counted in each locale setting; every timeout passed when its spec was re-run alone.
  - Locale unset: 349 passed; 5 hit the 30 s timeout under load; 10 did not run because they follow a failed test.
  - C.UTF-8: 360 passed; 1 timed out; 3 did not run.
  - My first C.UTF-8 run was stopped by my tool's 2-hour limit, not by a test. I kept its log and re-ran it in full.
- **My e2e probes:** in both locale settings, 0 failures across 546 + 77 + 14 checks per language. They cover accessibility (axe), 390 px width, 200 % text and auditor read-only views.
- **My older integration probes:** 4 of my own round-2/3 expectations now fail. Later decided ADR-0037 amendments (D-119, D-122) replaced them, so none is a product defect. My probe written against the current rules passes 5/5.
- **Validator:** register, pipeline and historical DG3/DG2/DG1 all pass.
- **Requirement trace:** all 137 rows are covered. The partial-coverage notes in the register are acceptable.

All failures and non-zero exits are explained in the record and in `RUN-NOTES.md`. No product gate G1–G6 was decided, and product G6 does not imply DG7.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG4/round-7/` and `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG4/qa/round-7/`:
- `qa-verifier.json`
- `qa-verifier.verifications.json`
- `qa-verifier.md`
- `RUN-NOTES.md`
